::: {.cards .two}
::: {.card-c}
[Starting point]{.tag}

### The problem

Governments subsidise cargo bikes, e-bikes, electric cars and energy-efficient retrofits. Part of the money goes to households that would have bought anyway, crowding out those who buy only when subsidised.
:::

::: {.card-c}
[Approach]{.tag}

### The solution

Households that would buy anyway tend to be more impatient and reluctant to wait for approval. A longer time between application and payment therefore shifts funds towards households whose purchase actually depends on the subsidy.
:::

:::

## The approach {#approach}

```{=html}
<ol class="steps">
<li><strong>Apply.</strong> Households apply for the subsidy as before.</li>
<li><strong>Set the waiting time.</strong> A waiting time separates application and payment; a uniform wait-time auction sets it so that as many households as possible are reached who buy only with support.</li>
<li><strong>Self-selection.</strong> Those who would buy anyway often buy right away without the subsidy. The funds remain for the households for whom they make the difference.</li>
</ol>
```
